source: Alfei, Miller, Ryan and Urcelay (2025) Rethinking memory impairments: Retrieval failure (preprint text, re-read for gaps 2, 6, 9)
finding: Gap 2: the review gives no count of reversal attempts that failed versus succeeded. Table 1 is a grid of recovery manipulations (time, physical context, state context, retrieval cue, US reactivation, optogenetic) by phenomenon, filled with citations of positive examples. Empty cells are marked X, meaning not tested, not failed.
numbers: No pooled effect, no n of studies, no tally. Table 1 note: the table presents noteworthy examples, not comprehensive.
quote: Table 1 also highlights instances in which such recovery has not been tested
limits: Selection of positive examples by advocates. A failure tally cannot be built from this paper.
agent_relevance: Treat the review as a map of cue types that have worked, not as a success rate. Do not quote a hit rate.

source: Alfei, Miller, Ryan and Urcelay (2025) Rethinking memory impairments: Retrieval failure (preprint text, re-read for gaps 2, 6, 9)
finding: Gap 2: the review states two limits itself. Recovery was not tested across wide parameter ranges, so absence of recovery may reflect parameter choice. Also, a test of the memory before the recovery manipulation can itself act as a reminder (Wheeler and Miller 2007), which affects how amnesia claims are read.
numbers: Applies to all cases where erasure is claimed. Also: no demonstrations found of recovery from proactive or retroactive outcome interference by US presentation (reinstatement) or by internal state (state-dependent retrieval).
quote: we did not find any demonstrations of recovery from proactive or retroactive outcome interference
limits: Text-level admission, no numbers.
agent_relevance: Some cue types have no positive evidence even in the favourable review. Do not assume every cue type revives every loss.

source: Alfei, Miller, Ryan and Urcelay (2025) Rethinking memory impairments: Retrieval failure (preprint text, re-read for gaps 2, 6, 9)
finding: Gap 6: the review itself lists failures in humans and animals: pharmacological cue-dependent amnesia failed to replicate in Luyten 2021, Schroyens 2019, Schroyens 2017, Stemerding 2022; non-pharmacological in Chalkia 2020 (two papers) and others; Walker motor-skill result fails in Hardwicke 2016; prediction-error extinction effects fail in Gerlicher 2022 and George 2024 (human).
numbers: About 8 named failure citations in the human section. No effect sizes given in the review.
quote: recent studies have sometimes failed to replicate pharmacological
limits: Citations only; I did not open each one.
agent_relevance: The human side of the retrieval-failure literature is mostly weak or contested. Do not build the agent on human erasure or human rescue effects.

source: Alfei, Miller, Ryan and Urcelay (2025) Rethinking memory impairments: Retrieval failure (preprint text, re-read for gaps 2, 6, 9)
finding: Gap 9: Table 1 column for optogenetic reactivation cites many studies: Ryan 2015, Roy 2016 (Alzheimer mice), Perusini 2017, Okuyama 2016, Kitamura 2017, Nabavi 2014, Redondo 2014, Abdou 2018, Guskjolen 2018, Poll 2020, Lacagnina 2019, Power 2023, O'Leary 2023, Autore 2023, Bolsius 2023, Chapman 2024.
numbers: 16 citations in the optogenetic column, spanning at least the Tonegawa, Ryan, Josselyn and Inokuchi groups; several share training lineage with Ryan. I did not verify each paper's result or whether each is a strict replication of Ryan 2015.
limits: Table is selective. Some cited papers (Redondo, Nabavi) concern memory valence or LTP, not amnesia rescue. Count of strict replications of Ryan 2015 stays unknown.
agent_relevance: Rodent engram rescue is a family of results from a few related labs, with one dissent (d05). Treat as moderate support, not a settled law.

source: Abdou et al. (2018) Synapse-specific representation of the identity of overlapping memory engrams, Science
finding: A counter-case to engram rescue. After complete retrograde amnesia of auditory fear conditioning in mice, light stimulation of auditory inputs to lateral amygdala failed to induce recall. The authors read this as the engram no longer existing in that circuit. Another linked memory in the shared cells was untouched. An erratum was issued in 2018.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC). Exact n not read.
quote: optogenetic stimulation of the auditory inputs to the lateral amygdala failed to induce memory recall
limits: Abstract only. Different amnesia route (a protocol for complete amnesia) from Ryan's anisomycin after one conditioning. Shows rescue is not universal.
agent_relevance: Some losses are real losses. A buried-fact strategy should allow that stored-but-unreachable is unproven when cues fail repeatedly.

source: Guskjolen et al. (2018) Recovery of lost infant memories in mice, Current Biology
finding: Optogenetic stimulation of tagged dentate gyrus neurons recovered lost infant memories in adulthood, up to 3 months after training. Supports retrieval failure for natural forgetting, from a lab other than the Tonegawa/Ryan pair.
numbers: Abstract read via Europe PMC; n not read.
limits: Abstract only. Artificial stimulation, not a natural cue. The author list is as cited in the Alfei Table 1 (Guskjolen 2018), not read from the abstract.
agent_relevance: Natural forgetting can be an access problem. Artificial cue reach is not available to a text agent, so only cue design transfers.

source: Hupbach, Gomez, Hardt and Nadel (2007) Reconsolidation of episodic memories: a subtle reminder triggers integration of new information, Learning and Memory
finding: Gap 6: a human cue-induced effect that does work, but it is intrusion, not erasure. A reminder before learning list 2 did not change items recalled from list 1, yet raised intrusions of list 2 items into list 1 recall on day 3. Not seen immediately (Exp 2), so time-dependent. No reminder effect on recall of list 2 (Exp 3).
numbers: Exp 1 three groups of 12 (F(2,33)); reminder vs no reminder intrusions Mann-Whitney U=20.00, p<0.01. Exp 3 N=24; intrusion rate from list 1 into list 2 about 5.4%, about one item of 20. Criterion 17 of 20 objects.
limits: Small groups. Intrusion is source confusion, not a change in memory strength. Other labs found impairment or no effect depending on conditions (Forcato 2007, 2010, per the review).
agent_relevance: A reminder cue can pull new items into the old trace. For an agent: recalling an old note while writing new content can contaminate it. Keep a source tag.

source: Kindt, Soeter and Vervliet (2009) Beyond extinction: erasing human fear responses and preventing the return of fear, Nature Neuroscience
finding: Gap 6: the other main positive human result. Propranolol before reactivation erased fear-potentiated startle 24 h later and prevented return of fear. It is the study behind the later propranolol replications and meta-analyses.
numbers: Abstract read via Europe PMC; no N or effect size in the abstract. Later: a healthy N=44 replication failed (b10).
quote: oral administration of the beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist propranolol before memory reactivation in humans erased the behavioral expression
limits: Effect size not obtained. Startle measure, healthy students, lab fear.
agent_relevance: Human erasure effects are drug and measure specific. No transfer to agent design.

source: Steenen et al. (2022) Updated and rectified meta-analysis shows no effect of propranolol versus placebo, J Psychiatry Neurosci (re-read)
finding: Gap 7 stays open. The letter reports the rectified pooled analysis (Hedges g, symptom severity) only as forest plots (Figures 1 and 2). The text gives no pooled g or CI. It says the interval is even wider after adding new and missed trials.
numbers: No pooled g or CI in the text. Page text is 14.7k characters.
quote: the 95 % confidence interval of the pooled mean difference is even wider
limits: Numbers sit in figures that cannot be read as text.
agent_relevance: Report the Steenen result as not significant with a wider interval, not as a number.

source: Lucki et al. (2025) An adversarial perspective on machine unlearning for AI safety: prompt-only attack (re-read for gap 1)
finding: Gap 1, partial: a prompt-only attack (enhanced GCG, a universal adversarial prefix) recovers a large part of unlearned knowledge with no weight update. Gaps to the base model remain.
numbers: WMDP-Bio, base 64.4: RMU 29.9 to 53.9, NPO 29.5 to 46.0, DPO 27.9 to 49.0. WMDP-Cyber, base 42.6: RMU 27.7 to 35.3, NPO 32.7 to 37.0, DPO 33.5 to 36.7.
limits: Prefix is an optimised adversarial string, not a natural encoding-context cue. Cyber gaps are small and noisy (paper's note). Read via fetch summary of first 100k characters.
agent_relevance: Pure-cue recovery of buried knowledge exists in LLMs. The cue is optimised, so a natural reinstatement cue may do less.

source: Lynch et al. (2024) Eight methods to evaluate robust unlearning in LLMs
finding: Gap 1, partial: on Llama-2-7B-Chat unlearned of Harry Potter, jailbreak prompts and in-context relearning (first lines of book 1 or summaries in context) raise familiarity, absolute and relative to the original, with no weight updates. Fine-tuning on 8000 sentences (about 10% of the corpus) brings it close to the original; 800 (1%) does less.
numbers: Familiarity baseline of the unlearned model 0.09. Trivia set 1239 questions. Exact post-prompt values only in figures. Rank-8 LoRA relearning.
quote: fine-tuning on 8,000 sentences brings the WHP model's performance close to the original
limits: Read via fetch summary. Increases described as modest. No test of reinstating the encoding framing.
agent_relevance: Supplying context content (a reminder) revives some buried knowledge. This is the closest LLM test of a reminder cue. Size is modest.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval: benchmarking chat assistants on long-term interactive memory, key expansion (gaps 3 and 8)
finding: Gaps 3 and 8: enriching the stored index key at write time (key = value plus extracted facts) raises retrieval at equal top-k. This is a cue-design test, not state matching.
numbers: LongMemEvalM Table 3: round K=V recall@5 0.582, @10 0.692, QA 0.615; round K=V+fact 0.644, 0.784, 0.657; session K=V 0.706, 0.783, 0.670; session K=V+fact 0.732, 0.862, 0.714. Averaged +9.4% recall@k and +5.4% QA accuracy. Retriever Stella V5 1.5B.
limits: Equal top-k, not equal tokens; fact keys cost indexing work. Read via fetch summary; appendix retriever comparison not read.
agent_relevance: Writing extra cue-like keys at storage time helps. Cheap for an agent: store a fact line next to each note.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval, time-aware query expansion (read-side cue rewrite)
finding: Gap 3: rewriting the query at read time with time ranges helps on the temporal subset, but only with a strong LLM. With Llama 3.1 8B it can hurt.
numbers: Temporal subset. Round recall@5/@10: K=V 0.421/0.499; +fact 0.489/0.550; +fact+GPT-4o expansion 0.526/0.722; Llama 8B expansion 0.481/0.570. Session recall@5 K=V 0.639, Llama 8B expansion 0.624 (drop). Average gain from expansion +11.3% round, +6.8% session.
limits: Temporal queries only. Not a multi-paraphrase or reverse-direction test. No token accounting.
agent_relevance: Query rewriting is a read-side cue and pays off only when the rewriter is strong. Equal-token comparison of repeated queries is still untested.

source: Ma et al. (2023) Query rewriting for retrieval-augmented large language models
finding: Gap 3: rewriting the query before retrieval gives small to moderate gains over plain retrieve-then-read. A trained rewriter adds more on some sets. Not a multi-query ensemble.
numbers: ChatGPT reader EM/F1. HotpotQA retrieve-then-read 30.47/41.34, LLM rewriter 32.80/43.85, trained 34.38/45.97. AmbigNQ 45.80/58.50, 46.40/58.74, 47.80/60.71. PopQA 43.20/47.53, 46.00/49.74, 45.72/49.51. MMLU STEM ChatGPT 63.3 to 63.5.
limits: No token or cost figures in the paper (checked). Bing web search, not a private memory store. On HotpotQA retrieve-then-read is below no retrieval (30.47 vs 32.36).
agent_relevance: One rewrite gives 0 to 3 points. Retrieval can even hurt (HotpotQA). Keep retrieval optional.

source: Chhikara et al. (2025) Mem0: production-ready AI agents with scalable long-term memory (LoCoMo)
finding: Gaps 3 and 8: on LoCoMo, a compact extracted-memory store beats plain chunk RAG at far fewer tokens but loses to full context. No test of state or context matching.
numbers: Overall J: Mem0 66.88 (1764 memory tokens), Mem0g 68.44 (3616), best RAG 60.97 (k=2, chunk 256), A-Mem 48.38 (2520), Zep 65.99 (3911), OpenAI 52.90 (4437), full context 72.90 (26031 tokens). Search p95 0.200 s for Mem0.
limits: Authors' own system; baselines re-run by the authors. RAG is not monotone in chunk size (k=1: 50.15 at 256, 36.84 at 4096), so tuning drives margins.
agent_relevance: Full context still wins on accuracy; stores win on cost. Write-time consolidation is the lever, not same-state retrieval.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: proactive interference in LLMs (mitigations, gap 4)
finding: Gap 4: telling the model to forget old values barely helps; no test deleted stale updates. A mock QA reset (a fake finished task before the query) helps most. So overwrite-versus-append at equal tokens is untested.
numbers: 46 keys, 3 to 400 updates per key, Qwen3-0.6B to DeepSeek-V3 (637B). Forget instruction: under 10 points gain at 100 updates, hurt gpt-4.1-mini. Mock QA reset: Gemini Flash 2.0 at 150 updates matched baseline at 30-45 updates. Size class predicts endurance (t=3.03, p=0.005, N=30); context length does not (p=0.886).
limits: Authors say the reset discards past associations, unsuitable when history is needed. Last 5.8k characters not read.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on ignore-earlier text. Test physically removing stale notes; no evidence yet. A framing reset is the only measured fix.

source: Gekhman et al. (2025) Inside-out: hidden factual knowledge in LLMs
finding: Gap 5: selecting among 1000 samples with an internal probe beats majority vote by a small margin; cross-dataset transfer is not tested.
numbers: Closed-book QA average accuracy: greedy 21.2, majority vote 22.0 (+3.9%), P(a|q) 22.3, probe 23.7 (+12.1%), probe with gold added 32.0, oracle 44.3. Probe per model: Llama 25.4, Mistral 22.0, Gemma 23.7. 12 model-relation settings, probe beats every external score in all 12 (p<0.05). 56% of questions have all 1000 samples wrong; in 9% the probe ranks the never-sampled gold first.
limits: One dataset (EntityQuestions, 4 relations), 3 models. 1000 samples per question is far above equal-token. No cross-dataset result in the text read; 45k characters unread.
agent_relevance: Gain over majority vote is about 1.7 points at 1000 samples. At equal tokens it is not shown to win.

source: Orgad et al. (2025) LLMs know more than they show: intrinsic representation of hallucinations
finding: Gap 5: probing the exact answer tokens detects errors well, but transfer across datasets is weak once a logit baseline is subtracted. Answer-selection results are in a figure only.
numbers: Error-detection AUC TriviaQA (Mistral-7B-Instruct / Llama3-8B-Instruct): probe on exact answer 0.85/0.83 vs logits-min-exact 0.75/0.79 and p(True) 0.66/0.73. Winobias 0.92/0.93 vs 0.59/0.61 for logits-min. Math 0.92/0.95. Error-type prediction AUC for consistently incorrect only 0.59 to 0.67.
quote: after subtracting the logit-min-exact baseline, the probe's gain rarely exceeds zero
limits: Four 7-8B models, 10 datasets; heatmap numbers not extractable. Needs hidden-state access.
agent_relevance: Internal scores detect errors but need white-box access and do not transfer. Not a general tool for an API agent.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language models (mostly) know what they know
finding: Gap 10: a feeling-of-knowing analogue exists. P(IK), trained on the bare question, predicts whether the model will answer correctly, before it generates. It is calibrated in distribution and degrades out of distribution.
numbers: 52B model. AUROC trained on TriviaQA only: TriviaQA 0.864, Mixed-Arithmetic 0.928, LAMBADA 0.606, Python 0.687, GSM8K 0.624. Trained on all tasks except GSM8K: 0.873, 0.987, 0.853, 0.881, 0.752. A relevant Wikipedia article raised P(IK) from 18% to 78% on one example. 30 samples at temperature 1 per question.
quote: P(IK) is very well calibrated on TriviaQA
limits: Needs training and logits. Zero- and few-shot P(IK) is poor. Underconfident out of distribution.
agent_relevance: A cheap detector for stored-but-unreachable is feasible only with a trained head. Without one, use agreement across rewrites as a proxy (untested).

source: Human cue-induced amnesia summary from the Alfei preprint (Hupbach 2007, Forcato 2007 and 2010)
finding: Gap 6 summary: the declarative human results the review cites show intrusion (Hupbach), impairment (Forcato 2007 when cue and response syllables matched) or no effect (Forcato 2010), depending on conditions. The fear results rest on propranolol (Kindt 2009) and Schiller 2010 retrieval-extinction, with failed replications.
numbers: No effect sizes in the review. Primary numbers obtained only for Hupbach 2007 (d07).
quote: new information presented in conjunction with cue-dependent amnesia treatment can either update or impair the original memory, or have no effect
limits: Second-hand from the preprint.
agent_relevance: Human effects depend on exact conditions. An agent should not expect a reminder to cleanly edit old content.
